newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Michelin, Bridgestone buy; Thai stocks haunt trade.
newsitem.headline: Michelin, Bridgestone buy; Thai stocks haunt trade.

text.p: Michelin, Bridgestone and possibly Goodyear engaged in buying for RSS3 and TSR20 rubber on Tuesday while news of large stocks held by Thailand spooked potential buyers in the market, dealers said.

"Bridgestone did something again in TSR20," a dealer said. "Michelin bought some RSS3 as part of their regular weekly purchases," another trader said. One dealer said U.S. giant Goodyear was "probably buying in the market."
But the market was more worried about the prospect that excess Thai stocks ranging between 120,000 to 150,000 tonnes may be sold in the market.
One trading house said that prospect "contributed to the dampness" in market demand and prompted some buyers to start asking for very low prices for some grades of rubber.

A trader said one major rubber firm was bidding for SIR20 rubber at a price of 43.00-43.25 U.S. cents/lb while offer prices at Medan were quoted a 44.00 cents. The same rubber house was looking for February RSS3 rubber at 100 U.S. cents.
At 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 94.00 U.S. cents a kg from 94.75 cents. September RSS1 was seen at 137.00 Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg from 139.00 cents.
